evals.prompt: I need a SQL view of open sales orders in Sage X3 with the sold-to customer name and the order total. The folder is SEED.
evals.expected_output: Reads INDEX.md, finds SORDER in table-index.md and its entry in dict/Sales.md. Builds the view on SEED.SORDER (schema = folder) joined to BPCUSTOMER / BPARTNER using the link expression on BPCORD ([BPR]BPR0 =[SOH]BPCORD) quoted from the dictionary, exposing only columns seen in dict/. Defines 'open' from the local menu behind ORDSTA (cited from the inline [menu N: ...] or local-menus.md), not a guess, and states the grain (one row per order). Delivers one CREATE OR ALTER VIEW in a sql block, notes tables/joins/status filter/assumptions, a TOP 20 sanity check, and cites the files.

evals.prompt: What table and field holds the allocation status on an X3 sales order, and what do the values mean?
evals.expected_output: Greps dict/Sales.md, names SORDER.ALLSTA (type M, local menu 416) and decodes the values from the dictionary (1=Not allocated, 2=Partly allocated, 3=Allocated), says which file it verified them in, notes that local menus can be customized per folder, and does not invent a column.

evals.prompt: Give me a query listing customers with their three address lines and whether they are active.
evals.expected_output: Finds the address-line field in dict/ with a (3) dimension and emits NAME_0, NAME_1, NAME_2 (not a single column). Treats the active flag as local menu 1 (1=No, 2=Yes), filtering/decoding on 2 for Yes rather than 1 or a bit. Cites the dictionary lines used.

evals.prompt: The client is on Sage X3 V12. Does SORDER have a column for the delivery address code?
evals.expected_output: Answers from the V11 dictionary (names the BPAADD field and its link expression), states clearly that the bundled dictionary is V11, and either fetches https://online-help.sagex3.com/erp/12/en-us/Content/MCD/SORDER.htm to confirm for V12 or tells the user to confirm there, rather than asserting V12 behaviour from memory.

evals.prompt: Write me a SQL statement that updates SORDER to close all orders older than 2020.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to write SQL that modifies X3 tables, explains that direct writes bypass X3's business logic (stock, accounting, sequence numbers, audit) and corrupt integrity, points to the application / import templates / web services as the correct path, and does not print the modifying statement even as an illustration.

evals.prompt: My X3 query 'WHERE SHIDAT IS NULL' returns no rows but I know many orders have no shipment date. Why?
evals.expected_output: Explains from conventions.md that X3 does not store SQL NULLs - on SQL Server the empty date is 1753-01-01 (1599-12-31 only on Oracle; and empty strings '' / numbers 0) - and gives the corrected predicate SHIDAT_0 > '1753-01-01' with the _0 suffix. Verifies the column exists in dict/ before using it.

evals.capability: dictionary / SQL (physical column names and date sentinel, must always pass)
evals.prompt: On SQL Server, give me a query of stock lines (STOCK) with item, site, quantity and the last count date, excluding lines never counted. Folder PROD.
evals.expected_output: Every referenced column carries the _0 suffix (ITMREF_0, STOFCY_0, QTYSTU_0, and the date column _0) - no bare dictionary names, except ROWID if used. The 'never counted' filter uses the SQL Server sentinel (> '1753-01-01' or a CASE that nulls it); the literal 1599-12-31 does not appear anywhere in the SQL. Columns are verified in dict/Stock.md and cited; schema is PROD.

evals.prompt: How do I write a 4GL script that posts a sales order in Sage X3?
evals.expected_output: Says this is not yet a bundled capability (development is planned), answers from Sage's official online help with a citation or says it cannot verify, does not invent 4GL API details, and notes that the skill could be extended.

evals.prompt: A client on Sage X3 V11 (SQL Server 2016, Windows Server 2016) wants to move to the current V12 release. What does it involve and will our reporting views break?
evals.expected_output: Pins source/target (names 2026 R1 = 12.0.39 as current per the guide and says to confirm on Sage's release-information post). States V11 is past end of maintenance (1 April 2024). From platform-matrix.md: Windows Server 2016 and SQL Server 2016 are not supported since 2026 R1, so the move needs new OS/DB (2019/2022/2025, SQL 2019/2022), MongoDB 8, JDK 11, PowerShell 7.2+ - which points to a folder upgrade rather than in-place. Gives the procedure in order (UU* controls, extract, import, activity codes, revalidation taking hours, post-upgrade). For views: additive default, lists tables touched from the release notes, offers diff_table_versions.py, includes the verification SQL with _0 suffixes. Cites Sage pages with dates.

evals.prompt: Is Sage X3 2025 R1 still supported, and when does it end?
evals.expected_output: Answers directly from the lifecycle section: 2025 R1 = 12.0.37, GA May 2025, 24-month maintenance (6 Current + 12 Standard + 6 Extended), in Standard stage per Sage's post read 2026-10-02, derived end of maintenance around May 2027 - and says to confirm the stage on Sage's Community release-information post. Does not give a full upgrade plan; one line on what moving to 2026 R1 would involve.

evals.prompt: Can we run Sage X3 2026 R1 on Windows Server 2025 with MongoDB on the same box?
evals.expected_output: From platform-matrix.md: Windows Server 2025 is supported since 2025 R1, but Sage's page (April 2025 note) says MongoDB 7/8 are not yet certified on Windows Server 2025 and recommends Windows Server 2022 for the MongoDB host; MongoDB 8 is mandatory from 2025 R2. Quotes the prerequisites page date (8 September 2026) and says to re-check the page because Sage re-issues it.

evals.prompt: We have a view on SORDER and SORDERQ for a client going from 2024 R2 to 2026 R1. Will it break?
evals.expected_output: Reads the release notes for 2025 R1, 2025 R2 and 2026 R1 (all skipped/target releases) and checks whether SORDER/SORDERQ appear in the 'tables whose dictionary definition changed' sections; runs or offers scripts/diff_table_versions.py SORDER SORDERQ; states the additive default (named columns keep working, SELECT * consumers break) and the real risks (local-menu values behind decoded statuses, dimension growth). Provides the sys.columns verification SQL with the _0 suffix and cites the files.

evals.prompt: When exactly was Sage X3 2026 R2 released and what's in it?
evals.expected_output: Does not invent a date or content: notes that the bundled references end at 2026 R1 (12.0.39, GA May 2026) and that a 2026 R2 would be expected around November 2026 per the bi-annual cadence; fetches Sage's release-notes archive (archive.json) or the Community release-information post to confirm, or says it cannot verify and tells the user where to check.
